name: Longest stretch with a given sum
brief: `nums` is a list of whole numbers, which may be negative or zero. Write `longest_sum_k(nums, k)`. It returns the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum is exactly `k`. It returns 0 if there is none.
constraints: $O(n)$ time is the target. Trying every start and end is too slow.
hint: A stretch ends at `i` with sum `k` when an earlier prefix sum equals the current one minus `k`. Store the first index of each prefix sum, and look up `total - k`.

examples.note: The last three entries, -1, 2 and 1, sum to 2. The first three, 4, -1 and 2, sum to 5. That is 3.
The only subarray sums to 5, not 4.

tests.call: [&]{ std::vector<int> v; for (int i = 0; i < 150000; ++i) { v.push_back(4); v.push_back(-4); } return longest_sum_k(v, 0); }()
[&]{ std::vector<int> v; for (int i = 0; i < 150000; ++i) { v.push_back(1); v.push_back(-1); } v.push_back(1); return longest_sum_k(v, 1); }()

how: Submit runs 14 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: The stretch ending at `i` has sum `k` when some earlier prefix sum equals `total - k`.
Keeping the first index of each prefix sum makes the stretch longest.
One pass with a hash map, so the work is $O(n)$.
